questions.lessonContent: Composer 2 is a specialized model designed for agentic software engineering, demonstrating strong long-term planning and coding intelligence while maintaining the ability to efficiently solve problems for interactive use. questions.lessonTitle: Understanding Software Engineering Agents and Their Environment
questions.lessonContent: Software engineering agents aim to autonomously act to solve a given task prompt. Given an environment (a codebase and an isolated container for code execution) along with a prompt giving the agent its task, an agent produces a rollout consisting of a series of actions, each of which makes one or more tool calls and yields responses. Tool calls may modify the underlying environment, and the result of a rollout is the final state of this environment. Composer 2 has access to a small set of general tools that allow it to read and edit files, run shell commands, search the codebase using grep or semantic search, and search the web. Its prompt includes a system message, the tool call format specification, recent file information, past user messages, and the current task.

questions.lessonTitle: KL Divergence Estimator in RL Training
questions.lessonContent: In Composer 2's reinforcement learning pipeline, KL divergence is used for regularization to control how much the updated policy deviates from the reference policy. The training uses the standard estimator k1 = -log r, where r(x) = p(x)/q(x), rather than the k3 estimator. While k3 is an unbiased estimator that reduces variance when p and q are close, research shows that its variance increases drastically as p and q diverge. This variance blow-up is particularly problematic for large KL values, which can occur during training. The k1 estimator does not suffer from this variance blow-up issue.

questions.lessonTitle: KL Divergence Estimation in Composer 2 Training
questions.lessonContent: Similar to prior work, Composer 2 uses a Kullback-Leibler divergence for regularization. Many open-source implementations of RL estimate KL with the estimator k3 = (r -1) - log r, which is an unbiased estimator that reduces variance when p and q are close. However, prior research shows that variance increases drastically as p and q diverge. For large KL values, the variance of the k3 estimate is extremely large. The k2 estimator does not suffer from variance blow-up but is biased. Therefore, Composer 2 uses the standard estimator k1 = -log r instead.
